]]> SpaceX cleared to deploy a million AI satellites as Musk looks towards a Kardashev Type II civilisation https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/fcc-approves-spacex-starmind-1-million-ai-satellites/ Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:02:00 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=58027 The US FCC has approved SpaceX’s Starmind project to deploy up to one million solar-powered AI satellites in orbit.

The post SpaceX cleared to deploy a million AI satellites as Musk looks towards a Kardashev Type II civilisation appeared first on AGN.

]]> The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorised SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) computing hardware, paving the way for what could become the largest satellite constellation ever assembled.

The approval, announced on 25 November, lets SpaceX proceed with its Starmind project, which aims to use solar energy collected in orbit to power space-based data centres and transmit the results of their computations back to Earth.

The US regulator has granted the first authorisation for a constellation of orbital data centres, amid growing concerns over the availability of electricity, land and water to support the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure on Earth.

However, SpaceX founder and chief executive Elon Musk has a much larger ambition for the project, one rooted in a scientific theory proposed by a Soviet astronomer more than six decades ago.

Musk sees orbital data centres as an early step towards humanity becoming a Kardashev Type II civilisation, a hypothetical society capable of harnessing the entire energy output of its host star.

The FCC itself referred to the concept in announcing its decision as its chairman Brendan Carr said, “More fundamentally, it ( the constellation of data centres in space) promises to bring the human race closer to a Kardashev II civilisation—one that can harness the full power of the sun.”

“This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth,” Carr said, adding, “Compute campuses or data centres are essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI. By moving compute capacity beyond Earth, SpaceX and the many competitors working on their own orbital data centres are meeting the moment.”

SI, or superintelligence, refers to artificial intelligence that would surpass human intellectual capabilities.

The regulator said the system also operates consistent with the FCC’s orbital debris rules, and that it is continuing to assess other proposals for orbital data centres.

What is SpaceX’s Starmind project?

Unlike SpaceX’s Starlink satellites, which primarily provide communications and internet connectivity, Starmind spacecraft are designed to process data in orbit.

Each satellite would effectively function as a small data centre, carrying computer processors, solar arrays, communications equipment and a system to dissipate the heat generated by its electronics.

Multiple satellites would be connected through high-speed optical links, allowing them to exchange information using lasers. Starlink would provide the communications network through which the results of AI computations could be transmitted back to users on Earth.

SpaceX has already unveiled its AI1 satellite design, which draws on technologies developed for its Starlink constellation.

According to specifications published by SpaceX, the spacecraft will feature a 210kW solar array with a power generation density of 250 watts per square metre. The solar technology is being manufactured by SpaceX in Bastrop, Texas.

The company has also designed the spacecraft to accommodate computing modules from different chip manufacturers, allowing it to take advantage of advances in semiconductor technology without being tied to a single supplier.

SpaceX is building a dedicated manufacturing facility, called Gigasat, in Bastrop. The company expects the facility to support the production and deployment of thousands of AI satellites starting as early as late 2027.

Why does SpaceX want to move data centres into space?

The expansion of AI has created a growing demand for electricity. Large terrestrial data centres require substantial amounts of power to operate their processors and cooling equipment. They also need land, access to electricity networks and, depending on their cooling systems, considerable quantities of water.

SpaceX believes it can overcome some of these constraints by moving the computing infrastructure into orbit, where solar energy can be collected without interference from clouds or the Earth’s atmosphere.

The company intends to operate its AI satellites in sun-synchronous orbits. These are orbits in which a satellite passes over locations on Earth at approximately the same local solar time. Carefully selected orbital configurations can provide near-continuous exposure to sunlight.

Cooling, however, presents a different engineering challenge in space.

Although the surrounding environment is cold, the absence of air means that heat cannot be carried away from electronic equipment through convection. Satellites instead rely on radiators to release waste heat as infrared radiation.

SpaceX claims its approach could reduce the power required for cooling by a factor of 10 compared with conventional terrestrial data centres.

The FCC authorisation also allows SpaceX to use radiofrequency communications as a backup to its optical network. Separate radio links will support emergency communications, spacecraft tracking and command functions.

What is the Kardashev scale?

In 1964, Soviet radio astronomer Nikolai Kardashev published a scientific paper titled Transmission of Information by Extraterrestrial Civilizations.

At the time, astronomers were investigating whether signals from technologically advanced extraterrestrial societies could be detected from Earth.

Kardashev approached the question by considering how much energy such civilisations might have at their disposal. The greater their energy resources, the more powerful their potential communications systems could be.

His classification subsequently became known as the Kardashev scale. In its widely used modern interpretation, it divides civilisations into three broad categories.

A Type I civilisation would be capable of exploiting energy resources on a planetary scale. In Earth’s case, this would encompass energy received from the Sun as well as other available resources.

A Type II civilisation would have access to the entire energy output of its host star, requiring infrastructure extending far beyond its home planet.

A Type III civilisation would be capable of harnessing energy on the scale of an entire galaxy, potentially drawing power from billions of stars.

American astronomer Carl Sagan subsequently refined the classification in the 1970s by introducing intermediate values, according to Britannica.

Why Musk wants to capture a millionth of the Sun’s energy

The Sun produces approximately 3.8 x 1026 W of power. Earth intercepts less than one two-billionth of that output, and humanity currently uses only a small fraction of the solar energy that reaches the planet.

Capturing even one-millionth of the Sun’s total output would provide approximately 380 trillion kilowatts of power, more than 1,000 times the total solar power intercepted by Earth.

Musk has used this comparison to illustrate the potential scale of energy generation beyond the planet.

“Our progress toward a Kardashev Type II civilisation, let’s have an aspiration that if we say that our goal is to get even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, that would be more than 1,000 times as much energy as could possibly be produced on Earth,” Musk said.

The Starmind project would operate on a considerably smaller scale.

The Starmind doesn’t envisage transmitting electricity back to Earth. The energy would be consumed by the spacecraft themselves.

Starship critical to SpaceX’s orbital data centre ambitions

Much of SpaceX’s ability to realise the Starmind project will depend on Starship, the company’s heavy-lift launch vehicle designed to be fully reusable.

Deploying one million satellites would require manufacturing and launch capabilities far beyond those currently available to the global space industry.

To put the number into perspective, approximately 28,800 satellites have been launched since the beginning of the space age in 1957, through about 7400 rocket launches, till early this year, according to figures cited by the European Space Agency (ESA).

SpaceX is targeting the third quarter of 2027 for the first Starmind satellite launches, according to reports.

SpaceX is also facing competition. Google, Starcloud, Blue Origin and Cowboy Space are among the companies exploring space-based computing. Google and Starcloud have already launched experimental AI satellites.

]]> NASA deploys P-3 Orion, Gulfstream III and King Air to monitor Iowa lead azide detonation https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/nasa-research-aircraft-iowa-lead-azide-detonation/ Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:13:00 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=57987 NASA mobilized three airborne research aircraft - a Lockheed P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III, and a Beechcraft King Air B200 - alongside its TEMPO satellite to collect atmospheric data during the US Army’s controlled detonation of 4.5 metric tonnes of unstable lead azide in Middletown, Iowa.

The post NASA deploys P-3 Orion, Gulfstream III and King Air to monitor Iowa lead azide detonation appeared first on AGN.

]]> NASA deployed three of its airborne research aircraft to Iowa this week to collect atmospheric and environmental data as the US Army carried out the controlled detonation of nearly 4.5 metric tonnes of unstable explosive material at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown.

A Lockheed P-3 Orion and a Gulfstream III from NASA’s Langley Research Center in Virginia were joined by a Beechcraft King Air B200 contracted by the agency’s Ames Research Center in California.

NASA also drew on observations from its space-based Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution (TEMPO) instrument as part of a coordinated federal response to the operation on 25 November.

The US Army had identified approximately 4,400kg of degraded lead azide that had become unstable during storage. The disposal operation raised concerns about the potential release of airborne lead particles.

A US Army spokesman said: “Today’s successfully controlled detonation exceeded expectations. Credit goes to our EOD professionals and the Soldiers on the ground today, with every indication showing the munitions used substantially reduced the lead azide threat and safely addressed the hazard. “

They added there was a reading of 0.0 lead detected on the ground after the detonation, explaining: “Immediate overhead coverage after the operation confirmed that everything targeted for removal was cleared, with no secondary explosions, no kickout, and no infrastructure damage on or around the installation.”

However, the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) said its air monitoring equipment had detected no airborne lead before, during or immediately after the detonation.

“All EPA air monitors continue to report a ZERO DETECT of airborne lead, which has remained consistent before, during, and after this morning’s controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant,” the agency said.

Around 300 EPA personnel were involved in collecting air, soil and water samples across the region. More than 1,200 samples had been collected before the detonation, with further samples being sent to laboratories for analysis.

NASA said it had “rapidly mobilized specialized research aircraft, space-based observation capabilities, and scientific personnel” to support the operation.

The deployment brought together three very different aircraft types, ranging from a 60-year-old former naval patrol aircraft to a converted business jet and a twin-engine general aviation turboprop.

All three types have been used extensively in airborne scientific research.

NASA’s 60-year-old P-3 Orion flying laboratory

The largest of the three aircraft deployed to Iowa is a former US Navy P-3 Orion built in 1966. Registered N426NA and designated NASA 426, the aircraft entered the agency’s airborne science programme in 1991.

Developed from the Lockheed L-188 Electra commercial airliner, the four-engine turboprop was designed for maritime patrol and anti-submarine warfare. Its long endurance and ability to operate at relatively low altitudes also made it suitable for atmospheric research.

NASA has used the aircraft to study weather systems, atmospheric chemistry, oceans, glaciers and polar ice. It also serves as a test platform for instruments being developed for future satellite missions.

The Orion has undergone extensive modifications since leaving military service. Openings have been incorporated into the upper and lower fuselage, allowing scientific instruments to make upward and downward-looking observations.

Seven cabin windows have been adapted to accommodate externally mounted experiments, while additional equipment can be fitted to the nose, tail and 10 mounting points on the wings.

Even the aircraft’s former weapons bay has found a new purpose. It can accommodate large scientific sensors and antennas or be configured to release atmospheric measuring devices known as dropsondes.

These instruments collect information on temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure and wind as they descend.

The P-3 can remain airborne for up to 12 hours, depending on its payload and weather conditions. It has a range of 3,800 nautical miles (7,038km), a useful payload of approximately 8,165kg and can accommodate up to 24 people, including its flight crew.

Despite its age, the aircraft has modern avionics and satellite communications equipment. Scientists can access meteorological information and aircraft position data during flight, while the communications network allows them to exchange information with other aircraft and ground teams.

Gulfstream III: From military transport to atmospheric research

NASA’s Gulfstream III also began its operational life as a military aircraft. In September 2017, NASA received authorisation to acquire three surplus C-20B Gulfstream III aircraft from the US Air Force. Two were allocated to support the agency’s spare parts requirements, while the third was assigned to scientific research.

The research aircraft, registered N520NA and designated NASA 520, arrived at Langley in December 2017, replacing the agency’s Dassault HU-25A Guardian.

The twin-engine business jet can accommodate a range of instruments designed to examine atmospheric composition and measure the distribution of airborne particles.

Among the instruments compatible with the Gulfstream III is NASA’s High-Altitude Lidar Observatory (HALO), which uses laser pulses to obtain information about water vapour, methane, clouds and aerosols beneath the aircraft.

Another instrument, the second-generation High Spectral Resolution Lidar (HSRL-2), allows scientists to examine the distribution and optical properties of airborne particles and clouds.

Unlike instruments that require an aircraft to fly directly through the air being sampled, lidar can make measurements remotely. Scientists can use the returning laser signals to establish how particles are distributed at different altitudes.

The Gulfstream III can also accommodate instruments that analyse the chemical composition of aerosols and measure individual soot particles.

NASA has not disclosed the precise combination of scientific instruments carried aboard the aircraft during the Iowa deployment.

Beechcraft King Air B200: A versatile research aircraft

The smallest aircraft involved in the operation was a Beechcraft King Air B200 operating under contract to NASA’s Ames Research Center.

The King Air 200 family dates back to the early 1970s, with the prototype making its first flight in October 1972. The B200 subsequently introduced more powerful engines and improved performance.

Widely used for business aviation, cargo transport and medical evacuation, the aircraft family also serves with the US military as the C-12 Huron utility transport.

NASA has been using B200 aircraft since the early 1980s, adapting them for a variety of aeronautical and environmental research programmes.

Its own modified King Air aircraft feature openings in the cabin floor through which cameras, radar equipment and laser-based instruments can make observations of the atmosphere, land or water below.

NASA’s Langley-based B200, for example, has additional mounting points beneath its wingtips for instruments that sample airborne particles.

A separate B200 operated by NASA’s Armstrong Flight Research Center has supported research into ocean circulation, soil moisture, snow cover and airflow over aircraft wings.

The relatively small size of the King Air makes it a practical choice for research missions that do not require the payload capacity or endurance of larger aircraft.

NASA has not identified the registration or detailed scientific configuration of the contracted B200 deployed to Iowa.

Monitoring air pollution from space

Complementing the three aircraft was NASA’s TEMPO instrument, which observes atmospheric pollution across North America from geostationary orbit.

Its measurements from geostationary orbit of ozone, aerosols, and clouds can create a dataset that provides understanding and improve prediction of air quality and physical risks on climate.

Unlike Earth observation satellites that pass over a particular location periodically, TEMPO can repeatedly observe the same geographical region throughout daylight hours.

Its measurements include nitrogen dioxide, ozone and formaldehyde, providing scientists with information about changes in atmospheric pollution.

Airborne instruments can supplement these observations by examining atmospheric conditions in greater detail over a specific area.

NASA has yet to release the scientific findings from its Iowa flights or specify the individual assignments undertaken by the three aircraft.

Jared Isaacman defends NASA’s involvement

NASA’s deployment also prompted an unusual exchange between the agency’s administrator, Jared Isaacman, and former US Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene.

Greene questioned NASA’s involvement on social media, compared the planned detonation to the Chernobyl nuclear disaster and disputed the Apollo Moon landings.

Isaacman dismissed the comparison, pointing out that the Iowa operation involved the controlled disposal of ageing explosive material rather than a nuclear reactor accident.

“In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation’s best on the field,” Isaacman wrote. “That is precisely why you call on NASA, putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work.”

He also responded to Greene’s remarks about the Apollo programme.

“And we did go to the Moon,” Isaacman wrote. “It is disheartening that this needs to be explained to a former member of Congress.”

]]> Norse Atlantic has suspended all flights and warned it will file for bankruptcy if it cannot find a short-term solution to its current cash crunch.

The development comes after the airline warned yesterday, 25 November, that its financial situation was ‘critical’.

In a statement, the airline said, “Under the circumstances, the Company has suspended all of today’s flights pending clarification as to whether a viable financing solution can be established for the Company. If a short-term financing solution is not secured urgently, it is the Board’s intention to file for bankruptcy.”

The airline was operating seven routes at the time of its suspension, with two more planned to start next month.

The routes Norse Atlantic has suspended

At the time of the suspension, Norse Atlantic was operating seven active routes, five of them to Thailand. Two more were due to launch in December, connecting Manchester to Bangkok and London Gatwick to Phuket.

Source: Cirium schedule data

Norse apologised to passengers but gave no details in its Thursday morning statement about refunds or alternative flights. The airline suspended all services scheduled for November 26 and has yet to say when flights might resume.

Pakistan International Airlines turns to its own aircraft after Norse flight suspension

Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) had been using Norse Atlantic’s Boeing 787-9s on its UK services. The airlines signed a wet-lease agreement in October for two Dreamliners to expand capacity between the UK and Pakistan.

Norse supplied the aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance, and the first 787 arrived in Islamabad on 1 November.

The disruption hit PIA on the evening of 25 November, hours before Norse announced the suspension of its own scheduled flights. PIA said passengers at Heathrow and Manchester were preparing to board when Norse told it without warning that it was suspending operations. PIA cancelled PK786 from London Heathrow to Islamabad and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore.

PIA said it would operate all UK flights with its own Boeing 777s from 26 November and was contacting passengers from the two cancelled departures to rebook them on later services.

]]> Ukraine uses laser weapon to shoot down jet-powered Russian Geran-4 drone https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/ukraine-laser-downs-russian-geran-4/ Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:02:00 +0000 https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/?p=57983 Ukraine has released footage that appears to show the first successful use of a laser weapon against a Russian jet-powered Geran drone.

The post Ukraine uses laser weapon to shoot down jet-powered Russian Geran-4 drone appeared first on AGN.

]]> The Ukrainian Telegram channel Serhii Flash has posted a video that appears to show a Russian Geran one-way attack drone being shot down. The engagement appears to represent the first publicly reported instance of a laser (directed energy weapon) being used to destroy a jet-powered attack drone.

The channel is owned by Serhii Beskrestnov, an adviser to the Ukrainian president on technology. The laser potentially offers a new class of short-range air defence for Ukraine.

Ukrainian laser appears to shoot down jet-powered Geran drone

The post said this was the work of Ukraine’s Blysk air defence laser systems, developed by the Ukrainian defence-tech company Carmine Sky. He wrote that the new laser system is “demonstrating first results under combat conditions.”

The video appears to show the laser system acquiring and tracking a jet-powered Geran-4 drone, and then engaging it with the laser system. The Geran seems to be at an altitude of around 400 metres and at a distance of almost 800 metres.

After the target is illuminated for several seconds, the drone tumbles out of the sky.

The laser is reportedly able to defeat small FPV drones in less than a second, but longer times are needed for larger Shahed-type drones.

For the first time, Ukrainian forces have shot down a Russian jet-powered attack drone using a laser weapons system. https://t.co/PV9xTu3pdk

— OSINTtechnical (@Osinttechnical) November 25, 2026

According to reporting cited by Militarnyi and the BBC, the turret-mounted system generates around 4 kW of output power and has an effective range of up to about a kilometre.

Carmine Sky’s website says about its laser efforts, “Laser counter-UAV system: Development of laser-based systems against aerial threats, including medium UAVs and Shahed-type targets.”

First publicly reported laser engagement against a jet-powered attack drone

This is believed to be one of the first publicly reported combat engagements involving a laser weapon against a jet-powered attack drone. Lasers have been used to neutralize small FPV drones, but it’s unclear if any country has successfully used them against jet-powered drones before.

The United States has several laser air defence systems, as do other countries like Israel. The Royal Navy is planning for its DragonFire to begin operational deployment on a Royal Navy Type 45 destroyer in 2027.

FAA approves anti-drone laser for US-Mexico border despite recent airspace shutdowns FAA approves anti-drone laser for US-Mexico border despite recent airspace shutdowns

Ukraine working on various laser air defence systems

Several Ukrainian companies are working to develop laser-based air defence systems under Ukraine’s ‘Private Air Defence’ programme.

Ukraine’s air defence systems and layers are now incredibly diverse, ranging from high-end interceptor missiles to machine guns mounted onto utility helicopters.

Beskrestnov cautioned that it is too early to discuss serial production of Carmine Sky’s laser system. Testing remains ongoing, during which time the lasers are already protecting critical infrastructure.

Lasers are often poorly understood in popular imagination. They are not next-generation technologies that will render existing air defence obsolete.

Instead, they are better understood as another layer of air defence that complements other layers. They are not “wonder weapons,” although they are seen as an important layer of air defence in next-generation systems.

It is partly for systems like lasers that 6th-generation fighter jets and warships are being designed with surplus power generation.

Lasers have some advantages, but they are also plagued by disadvantages such as being restricted to line-of-sight engagements, high power requirements, reduced effectiveness in cloudy weather, and the need to focus on a target for several seconds to achieve an effect.

.sie-field-hero{position: relative; 
 left: 50%;
 right: 50%;
 margin-left: -50vw;
 margin-right: -50vw;
 width: 100vw; 
 min-height: 480px;
 max-height: 560px;
 background-size: cover;
 background-position: center 40%;
 background-repeat: no-repeat; 
 background-color: #003B73;
 overflow: hidden;
 margin-bottom: 0;}
.sie-field-hero--no-image{background: linear-gradient(
 135deg,
 var(--field-color, #003B73) 0%,
 color-mix(in srgb, var(--field-color, #003B73) 65%, #000) 100%
 );}
.sie-field-hero__bg-img{position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center 40%;
 z-index: 0;
 display: block;}
.sie-field-hero__overlay{position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 1;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.90) 0%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.60) 38%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.25) 65%,
 rgba(0, 20, 50, 0.12) 100%
 );
 display: flex;
 align-items: flex-end;
 padding-bottom: 52px;}
.sie-field-hero__inner{width: 100%;
 max-width: 1100px;
 margin: 0 auto;
 padding: 0 32px;}
.sie-field-hero__label{display: block;

 font-weight: 500;
 color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.75);
 margin-bottom: 12px;
 letter-spacing: 0.03em;}
.sie-field-hero__label a{color: inherit;
 text-decoration: none;}
.sie-field-hero__label a:hover{color: #fff;
 text-decoration: underline;}

 margin-bottom: 14px;

 letter-spacing: 0.03em;}
.sie-field-category-badge i{font-size: 11px;

.sie-field-hero__title{font-size: clamp(30px, 5vw, 54px);

/* At a glance */
.sie-ovv{border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}

.sie-ovv__bar > *{background:#12233D !important;border-right:2px solid #fff}

.sie-ovv__bar > *:nth-child(3){background:#6B7A8F !important}

.sie-ovv__chip:hover{border-color:#12233D !important}
.sie-ovv__chip.is-active{background:#12233D !important;border-color:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__chip.is-active i{color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__basis-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;font-family:inherit !important;font-weight:600 !important}
.sie-ovv__basis-btn.is-on{background:#12233D !important;color:#fff !important}
.sie-ovv__basis{border:1px solid #C3C9CE !important;border-radius:4px !important;overflow:hidden}
/* Flow area and card names */

.sie-flow__summary{color:#4A525C !important}
.sie-flow__source-pill{box-shadow:none !important}

body .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}

body .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
body .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px !important}
body .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px !important}

/* ── Resources pages (2026-11-09) ── */
/* Breadcrumb (Breadcrumb plugin, theme2): plain text trail instead of boxed links. */
.breadcrumb-container ol{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;list-style:none;margin:0 0 14px !important;padding:0 !important}
.breadcrumb-container li{display:inline-flex;align-items:center}
.breadcrumb-container li a{background:none !important;border:0 !important;box-shadow:none !important;padding:4px 0 !important;margin:0 !important;border-radius:0 !important;font-size:13px;color:#4A525C !important}
.breadcrumb-container li a span{color:inherit !important}
.breadcrumb-container li a:hover{color:#12233D !important;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}
.breadcrumb-container li:last-child a{color:#12233D !important;font-weight:600}
.breadcrumb-container li:not(:last-child)::after{content:"\203A";margin:0 9px;color:#9A958A;font-size:14px}
.breadcrumb-container .separator{display:none !important}
/* Full-width pages (e.g. /in-english) print the trail in a bare<nav>; give it the content column. */
nav > .breadcrumb-container{max-width:1080px;margin:0 auto;padding:14px 24px 0;box-sizing:border-box}
/* Grades + Tuition fees: no glowing orbs, no gradients, navy calls to action. */
.gr-orb,.tuition-orb{display:none !important}
.gr-universe,.tuition-universe{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8}
.gr-card-header,.tuition-card-header{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #E4E0D8}
.gr-ects-inner,.sie-content details{background:#fff !important;background-image:none !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-inner,.leo-tuition-cta-inner{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-btn,.leo-tuition-cta-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border:1px solid #fff !important;border-radius:4px !important;font-weight:600 !important;box-shadow:none !important}
.gr-leo-cta-btn:hover,.leo-tuition-cta-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED !important}
.tuition-card-leo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important}
/* Grade bands keep their meaning (A best → F fail) as a thin coloured rule on a
 neutral row, instead of five pastel fills. */
.gr-grade{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border-left:3px solid #C3C9CE;border-radius:3px !important}
.gr-grade-a{border-left-color:#4F8A62 !important}.gr-grade-b{border-left-color:#86A05A !important}.gr-grade-c{border-left-color:#C2A243 !important}.gr-grade-d{border-left-color:#C7843F !important}.gr-grade-f{border-left-color:#B0554B !important}
.gr-ects-pill{background:#FAF8F4 !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8 !important;border-left-width:3px !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:3px !important}
.gr-ects-a{border-left-color:#4F8A62 !important}.gr-ects-b{border-left-color:#86A05A !important}.gr-ects-c{border-left-color:#C2A243 !important}.gr-ects-d{border-left-color:#C7843F !important}.gr-ects-f{border-left-color:#B0554B !important}

 Schengen): one readable column, a real type scale and proper tables. */

 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat-label{margin-top:8px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.3px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#4F5967}
 @media(max-width:700px){
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stats-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))}
 .lh-stats--figures .lh-stat:nth-child(2){border-right:0}
 }
 /* Monogram instead of a repeated building glyph. Hairline tile, serif
 letters — it reads as a placeholder somebody chose, not as missing data. */
 .lh-uni-logo-placeholder{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:#F4F2ED;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:5px;color:#8A8578}
 .lh-uni-monogram{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:22px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1px;color:#12233D}
 /* ── For institutions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 The one full navy band on the page. It is dark on purpose: it marks a
 change of audience, so a student scrolling past knows at a glance that
 this part is not addressed to them. */
 .lh-inst{background:#12233D;color:#fff}
 .lh-inst-wrap *,.lh-inst-wrap *::before,.lh-inst-wrap *::after{box-sizing:border-box}
 .lh-inst-inner{max-width:1200px;margin:0 auto;padding:clamp(48px,6vw,88px) clamp(16px,4vw,48px);display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1.35fr) minmax(0,1fr);gap:clamp(28px,4vw,64px);align-items:start}
 .lh-inst-badge{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-h{margin:0 0 16px;font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-size:clamp(26px,3.1vw,40px);line-height:1.16;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.5px;color:#fff;max-width:20ch}
 .lh-inst-body{margin:0 0 26px;font-size:clamp(15.5px,1.4vw,17px);line-height:1.65;color:#C6D2E0;max-width:54ch}
 .lh-inst-actions{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px}
 .lh-inst-btn{display:inline-block;text-decoration:none;background:#fff;color:#12233D;font-size:15.5px;font-weight:600;padding:14px 26px;border:1px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;min-height:44px}
 .lh-inst-btn:hover{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#44597A;font-weight:500}
 .lh-inst-btn--ghost:hover{background:none;color:#fff;border-color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-terms{margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}
 .lh-inst-terms li{border-top:1px solid #28405F;padding:20px 0}
 .lh-inst-terms li:first-child{border-top:0;padding-top:0}
 .lh-inst-k{margin:0 0 6px;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:19px;color:#D7A83F}
 .lh-inst-v{margin:0;font-size:15px;line-height:1.6;color:#C6D2E0}
 @media(max-width:860px){
 .lh-inst-inner{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 }
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-portals--search{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-res-list{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-herosearch .sie-flow__branches{grid-template-columns:1fr}
 .lh-heroalt{flex-direction:row;flex-wrap:wrap}
 .lh-heroalt-card{flex:1 1 220px}
 .lh-hero-scrim{background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(250,248,244,.97) 0%,rgba(250,248,244,.93) 62%,rgba(250,248,244,.72) 100%)}
 }
 /* ── Institutional pass, part 2 (2026-11-08, evening) ──────────────────
 Brings the sections below the hero onto the palette and type the hero
 already uses, so the page reads as one document instead of two designs
 stacked on top of each other. Everything here is homepage-only (it lives
 in this template) and is pure CSS: delete this block to revert. */
 /* The page itself: the site-wide body is cold pale blue (#E8F1FA), which
 showed through every transparent section (the institutions carousel and
 the study fields block) as a blue band between warm ones. */
 body.page-id-150{background:#FAF8F4}
 /* ⚠️ THE HEADLINE NEVER WAS SERIF. leonardo-homepage-css.min.css carries
 `.lh-wrap .lh-title{font-family:system-ui !important; font-size:44px
 !important; font-weight:800 !important; color:#003b73 !important}`, so
 the Source Serif rule earlier in this block lost on every device. Only
 !important with equal-or-higher specificity can beat it. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title,.lh-wrap .lh-hero h2.lh-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(34px,4.4vw,58px) !important;line-height:1.08 !important;letter-spacing:-.6px !important;color:#12233D !important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D !important}
 /* The accent word: italic navy reads editorial; bright orange read promo. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-gradient-text{color:#12233D;-webkit-text-fill-color:#12233D;font-style:italic;font-weight:600}
 /* One label above the headline is enough. The H1 eyebrow ("STUDY IN
 EUROPE") already does that job; the extra pill only added noise. */
 .lh-hero .lh-badge{display:none}
 /* Phones: the hero had no side gutter, so the eyebrow sat flush against
 the screen edge while the centred text did not. Left-aligned, with the
 same 20px gutter as the rest of the page, it matches the desktop. */
 @media(max-width:900px){
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-center{padding-left:20px;padding-right:20px;box-sizing:border-box;text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-hero-text,.lh-hero .lh-subtitle{text-align:left}
 .lh-wrap .lh-hero .lh-title{text-align:left}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 }
 /* ── Section headers: same voice as the institutions band ─────────────
 Serif headings and a small monospaced label instead of the rounded blue
 pills, which were the last "app" element on the page. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-header h2{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif !important;font-weight:600 !important;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px) !important;letter-spacing:-.4px;line-height:1.15;color:#12233D !important}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-badge{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:14px;padding:0;background:none;border-radius:0;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:500;letter-spacing:1.8px;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8C5A23}
 .lh-wrap .lh-section-sub{color:#4A525C}
 /* Section rhythm: paper / white / paper, so each block has an edge. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-how{background:#FAF8F4}
 .lh-wrap .lh-unis{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins{background:#fff;border-top:1px solid #E4E0D8}
 /* How it works: the three steps were top-aligned, so the middle card
 (longer text) hung lower than its neighbours. Stretch evens them. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-steps{align-items:stretch}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step{background:#fff;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-num{background:#12233D;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,monospace;font-weight:500}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-icon{background:#F4F2ED;color:#12233D;border-radius:6px}
 .lh-wrap .lh-step-arrow{color:#B7B1A5}
 /* Cards: tighter corners and hairlines everywhere. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card{border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--origins [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px;border-color:#E4E0D8;box-shadow:none}
 .lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries a[class*="card"],.lh-wrap .lh-dest-section--countries [class*="card"]{border-radius:6px}
 /* ── Study fields block (rendered by [sie_study_fields] after .lh-wrap) ─
 Six bright category colours, gradient pills and a gradient CTA made it
 the loudest part of the page. Same content, one navy, warm neutrals.
 The branch colours arrive as INLINE custom properties and inline
 backgrounds, so these overrides need !important to apply. Scoped to the
 homepage: the study-field pages keep their colour coding. */
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-title{font-family:"Source Serif 4",Georgia,serif;font-weight:600;font-size:clamp(28px,3vw,40px);letter-spacing:-.4px;color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-subtitle{color:#4A525C}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__source-pill{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;box-shadow:none !important;border-radius:4px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__junction-dot{background:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch{--branch-color:#12233D !important;--branch-bg:#F4F2ED !important;border:1px solid #E4E0D8;border-radius:6px;box-shadow:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-accent{display:none}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-icon{background:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__branch-count{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card{background:#FAF8F4;border:1px solid #EDEAE3;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-card:hover{border-color:#12233D}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__field-icon{background:#F4F2ED !important;color:#12233D !important;border-radius:5px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-flow__leo-link{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leonardo{background:#12233D !important;background-image:none !important;border-radius:6px}
 body.page-id-150 .sie-fields-leo-btn{background:#fff !important;color:#12233D !important;border-color:#fff !important;border-radius:4px}
 /* Alignment: the search widget carries its own 24px side padding, so the
 bar sat indented from the headline above it; and the trust row was
 centred under a left-aligned column. Both now share the text's edge.
 Only the LEFT padding goes: removing the right one too pushed the
 "AI-enhanced matching" toggle across the seam into the navy side. */
 .lh-herosearch .sie-sps-wrap{padding-left:0 !important}
 .lh-hero .lh-trust-row{justify-content:flex-start}
 /* Institution cards: the stylesheet tints each card top a different pastel

 monogram or logo is the only thing that differs between cards. */
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-card:nth-child(n) .lh-uni-card-top{background:#F4F2ED !important;background-image:none !important;border-bottom:1px solid #EDEAE3}
 .lh-wrap .lh-uni-cta{color:#0B5FA5 !important}
 .lh-wrap .sie-dest-hub__name{color:#12233D}

 DESTINATIONS PANEL  — overlay + grid
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
 /* Outer layer: covers full viewport */
 .sie-dest-panel {
 position: fixed;
 inset: 0;
 z-index: 2147483000;
 display: flex;
 align-items: stretch;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 opacity: 0;
 visibility: hidden;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .25s ease, visibility .25s;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open {
 opacity: 1;
 visibility: visible;
 pointer-events: auto;
 }
 /* Backdrop */
 .sie-dest-panel__backdrop {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 background: rgba(11, 55, 112, .52);
 backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(3px);
 cursor: pointer;
 }
 /* Sheet — right-panel on desktop */
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 position: relative;
 z-index: 1;
 width: min(800px, 100%);
 height: 100%;
 background: #fff;
 overflow-y: auto;
 -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch;
 padding: 26px 26px 40px;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 gap: 0;
 transform: translateX(28px);
 opacity: 0;
 transition: transform .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), opacity .38s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
 box-shadow: -20px 0 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateX(0);
 opacity: 1;
 }
 /* Mobile: bottom-sheet */
 @media (max-width: 767px) {
 .sie-dest-panel {
 align-items: flex-end;
 justify-content: stretch;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 width: 100%;
 height: 92vh;
 border-top-left-radius: 22px;
 border-top-right-radius: 22px;
 padding: 20px 16px 40px;
 transform: translateY(28px);
 box-shadow: 0 -16px 48px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
 }
 .sie-dest-panel.open .sie-dest-panel__sheet {
 transform: translateY(0);
 }
 }
 /* ── Header ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__header {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 justify-content: space-between;
 margin-bottom: 6px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__titlewrap {
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 10px;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__globe {
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #1e66f5;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__title {
 font-size: 1.5rem;
 font-weight: 800;
 color: #0b3770;
 margin: 0;
 line-height: 1.2;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close {
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 font-size: 22px;
 color: #0b3770;
 cursor: pointer;
 padding: 6px 8px;
 border-radius: 8px;
 line-height: 1;
 opacity: .75;
 transition: opacity .15s, background .15s;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__close:hover {
 opacity: 1;
 background: #f0f4ff;
 }
 /* Subheading */
 .sie-dest-panel__sub {
 color: #466087;
 font-size: .94rem;
 margin: 0 0 20px;
 flex-shrink: 0;
 }
 /* ── Country grid ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 display: grid;
 grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr);
 gap: 14px;
 /* allow this to grow and scroll */
 flex: 1;
 align-content: start;
 }
 @media (max-width: 620px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
 gap: 10px;
 }
 }
 @media (min-width: 621px) and (max-width: 860px) {
 .sie-dest-panel__grid {
 grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
 }
 }
 /* ── Country card ── */
 .sie-dest-panel__card {
 position: relative;
 display: block;
 aspect-ratio: 3 / 2;
 border-radius: 12px;
 overflow: hidden;
 text-decoration: none;
 background: #1d3557;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card--no-img .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 background: linear-gradient(135deg, #1d3557 0%, #1e66f5 100%);
 }
 /* Hero image layer — scales on hover */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 transition: transform .4s ease;
 will-change: transform;
 }
 /* <img> fills the card exactly like background-size:cover did.
 loading="lazy" means the browser only fetches each image when the
 panel opens and the card enters the viewport — saving ~30 MB of
 upfront image requests on every page that includes this panel. */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-img {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 width: 100%;
 height: 100%;
 object-fit: cover;
 object-position: center;
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-bg,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-bg {
 transform: scale(1.07);
 }
 /* Gradient overlay + text */
 .sie-dest-panel__card-body {
 position: absolute;
 inset: 0;
 display: flex;
 flex-direction: column;
 justify-content: flex-end;
 padding: 10px 12px 10px;
 background: linear-gradient(
 to top,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .72) 0%,
 rgba(0, 0, 0, .30) 55%,
 transparent 100%
 );
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-name {
 color: #fff;
 font-weight: 700;
 font-size: .92rem;
 line-height: 1.2;
 text-shadow: 0 1px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
 display: block;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 display: block;
 color: rgba(255,255,255,0);
 font-size: .75rem;
 margin-top: 2px;
 transition: color .2s ease, transform .2s ease;
 line-height: 1;
 }
 .sie-dest-panel__card:hover .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow,
 .sie-dest-panel__card:focus-visible .sie-dest-panel__card-arrow {
 color: rgba(255,255,255,.9);
 transform: translateX(4px);
 }
 /* ── Body-scroll lock ── */
 body.sie-dest-panel-open {
 overflow: hidden;
 }
 /* ── Country interest heart ── */
 .sie-country-heart {
 position: absolute;
 top: 8px;
 right: 8px;
 z-index: 10;
 background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.88);
 border: none;
 border-radius: 20px;
 padding: 4px 8px 4px 7px;
 display: flex;
 align-items: center;
 gap: 4px;
 cursor: pointer;
 font-size: 13px;
 color: #94a3b8;
 box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,.22);
 backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(6px);
 transition: color .18s, transform .18s, background .18s;
 line-height: 1;
 min-width: 28px;
 justify-content: center;
 }
 .sie-country-heart:hover {
 transform: scale(1.12);
 background: #fff;
 color: #ef4444;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted {
 color: #ef4444;
 background: #fff;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.voted i {
 animation: sie-heart-pop .35s cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97);
 }
 @keyframes sie-heart-pop {
 0%   { transform: scale(1); }
 40%  { transform: scale(1.45); }
 70%  { transform: scale(.88); }
 100% { transform: scale(1); }
 }
 .sie-country-heart__count {
 font-size: 11px;
 font-weight: 700;
 color: inherit;
 display: none;
 }
 .sie-country-heart.has-votes .sie-country-heart__count {
 display: inline;
 }
 /* ── Trigger button styles (for use in any menu) ── */
 /* Desktop globe icon */
 .se-dest-desktop-btn {
 font-size: 24px;
 color: #fff;
 text-decoration: none;
 cursor: pointer;
 transition: transform .2s, color .2s;
 position: relative;
 line-height: 1;
 background: transparent;
 border: 0;
 padding: 0;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover {
 transform: scale(1.15);
 color: #FFCC00;
 }
 /* Tooltip on desktop */
 @media (min-width: 1024px) {
 .se-dest-desktop-btn::after {
 content: "Study Destinations";
 position: absolute;
 bottom: -30px;
 left: 50%;
 transform: translateX(-50%);
 background: #007BFF;
 color: #fff;
 padding: 4px 8px;
 font-size: 12px;
 border-radius: 5px;
 opacity: 0;
 pointer-events: none;
 transition: opacity .2s;
 white-space: nowrap;
 }
 .se-dest-desktop-btn:hover::after {
 opacity: 1;
 }
 }
 /* Mobile pill button */
 .se-dest-btn {
 background: #0b3770 !important;
 color: #fff !important;
 }
 .se-dest-btn:hover {
 background: #1e66f5 !important;

<h1 class="title-h1 eac-page-title">Conference on the Future of Europe : the future is in your hands</h1>
<span><span>sandoel</span></span>
<span><time datetime="2021-12-07T08:55:30+01:00" title="Tuesday, December 7, 2021 - 08:55">Tue, 12/07/2021 - 08:55</time>
</span>
<div class="ecl"><h2><strong>What is the Conference?</strong></h2>

<p>The <strong>Conference on the Future of Europe </strong>is the first transnational discussion with Europeans on how to address Europe’s challenges together. This is an opportunity to think about what citizens and&nbsp; civil society want for the European Union.</p>

<p>&nbsp;</p>
</div>

                                                                <div class="video-description lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><div><p>The European Parliament, the Council, and the European Commission have committed to listen and follow up on the recommendations made</p></div></div>

<div class="lc-padding-top-half lc-padding-bottom-default lc-background-color-white lc-contained eac-stripe eac-stripe--bg-white" id="paragraph-827">  <div class="eac-stripe__inner">            <div class="full-html-body">
  <div class="eac-body lc-stripe-wrapper-text"><h2><strong>How does the Conference work?</strong></h2>

<p>Europeans can share ideas via the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Multilingual Digital Platform</a>, and both national and&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/assemblies/citizens-panels" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">European Citizens' Panels</a>. These contributions feed into the&nbsp;<a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/plenary" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference Plenaries</a>.</p>

<p>The Conference&nbsp;offers a new public forum for an open, inclusive, and transparent debate with citizens around a number of key priorities and challenges.</p>

<h2><strong>How can you participate?</strong></h2>

<ul>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]--><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/processes?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">share your own ideas or support others’ ideas</a> on the multilingual digital Conference platform</li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->organise your own events and promote it by adding them to the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/?locale=en&amp;pk_source=pdf_document&amp;pk_medium=link&amp;pk_campaign=europarl" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Conference platform</a></li>
	<li><!--[if !supportLists]--><!--[endif]-->take a look at the <a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/meetings" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">events organised by people across the EU</a></li>
</ul>

<h2><strong>What will the outcome be?</strong></h2>

<p>All of the ideas gathered and reports on events are published on the platform openly and transparently. These reports will then directly influence the discussions in the European Citizens’ Panels as well as in the Plenaries, where citizens will enter into a dialogue with national and European decision makers.</p>

<p>By spring 2022, the Conference will provide guidance on the future of Europe to the European institutions</p>

<p><a href="https://futureu.europa.eu/pages/getinvolved" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">Get involved and make your voice heard when it comes to education, culture, youth, sport, and more</a>.</p>

<p>Follow on Twitter at&nbsp;</p>

<ul>
	<li><a class="external-link eac-external-link" href="https://twitter.com/search?q=%23TheFutureIsYours" rel="nofollow" target="_blank">#TheFutureIsYours</a></li>
	<li><a href="https://twitter.com/search?q=%23#FutureofEurope" target="_blank" class=" eac-external-link">#FutureofEurope</a></li>
</ul>

Role overview

We are hiring Senior Account Executives for inbound and outbound sales opportunities. You will help real estate investors understand our platform, choose the right solution for their budget, and become long-term customers.

In an inbound role, you will work with warm leads and meetings generated by our marketing team and AI callers. In an outbound role, you will build relationships with investors through proactive outreach. Across both, you will own your pipeline, follow up consistently, and grow revenue from new and existing customers.

This is a remote, full-time role working US hours. Strong performers can grow into management, build teams, and help shape how we sell.

Responsibilities

  • Run discovery calls and product demos with real estate investors; understand their goals and recommend a solution that fits their needs and budget.

  • Convert booked meetings, new sign-ups, and warm leads into customers through timely calls, texts, and emails.

  • Generate additional meetings through proactive outreach and disciplined follow-up.

  • Close on the first call when appropriate, or agree on a clear next step and follow through.

  • Develop existing accounts through regular check-ins, relevant upsells, and lasting customer relationships.

  • Maintain consistent follow-up while respecting opt-outs and customer preferences.

  • Keep accurate CRM records for every meeting, deal, and follow-up, and report on activity and results daily.

  • Meet and exceed revenue targets, and apply coaching and feedback to improve your performance.

Requirements

  • Strong motivation to sell, close business, and deliver measurable results.

  • Ability to build trust quickly, understand customer needs, and communicate product value clearly.

  • Proactive pipeline ownership and consistent follow-through from first contact to a clear outcome.

  • Openness to direct feedback and the ability to put it into practice quickly.

  • Confidence working remotely, managing your calendar, and taking responsibility for your results.

  • Availability to work US hours.

Nice to have

  • Knowledge of real estate investing, wholesaling, proptech, or lead generation. Real estate experience is helpful but is not required; we provide training.

Compensation

  • First-year on-target earnings (OTE): $120,000–$150,000, including base salary and commission.

  • Top performers earn $200,000+ annually.

  • Competitive base salary, negotiable based on experience.

  • Uncapped revenue-based commission, paid every two weeks.

  • Our current top representative averages more than $13,000 per month in commission, in addition to base salary.

What we offer

  • A product built for real estate investors, with solutions for different customer budgets.

  • Warm leads and booked meetings, alongside opportunities to develop your own pipeline and grow existing accounts.

  • Structured onboarding, product training, tools, and direct feedback from day one.

  • AI tools for call analysis, sales practice, and coaching.

  • Opportunities to grow into sales management and help build a team.

  • Support for developing your professional profile in the real estate industry.

  • Remote work with US working hours.

  1. Submit your application.

  2. Screening call with our recruiter.

  3. Interview with our VP of Sales.

  4. Offer decision or clear, useful feedback.

  5. Want to skip the line? Apply through our fast track: short form, short video, then an AI interview on the spot. Pass it and you meet the VP of Sales for the final interview within 5 business days.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical / engineering leadership interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

🚀 EverAI — Building the Future of AI Companionship

At EverAI, we’re shaping what it means to connect with AI. With 60 million users and counting, we're not just building products — we're creating entirely new categories.

Our flagship product is the world’s largest AI companionship platform, redefining relationships for millions. It is governed by our proprietary moderation system, EverGuard — an internal AI designed to ensure everything we build is safe, ethical, and human-first.

And we’re only just getting started!

Alexis Soulopoulos [CEO]

• 10+ years in Tech Executive Leadership

Your Role

We scaled to 50 million users in just 2 years with a lean team of 100 people. Last year, we doubled our headcount.

Now, we’re scaling again, and the next hires will shape what EverAI looks like at 100+ people. As our third Talent Acquisition Specialist, you’ll be central to that build, as you’re joining at a defining stage.

You’ll work closely with our CEO, Alexis, and partner with leaders across the business to help assemble the team behind one of the fastest-growing AI products globally. We hire internationally and across every function of the company, with a strong focus on tech, bringing together people from leading tech hubs around the world.

You’ll also have the opportunity to influence how Talent Acquisition evolves as we grow: refining our internal workflows, experimenting with new AI tools, launching employer branding initiatives, testing sourcing strategies that keep our quality bar high, and so on.

Key Mission

Identify, attract, and land top global talent, while helping build a recruitment stack that matches the scale and ambition of a company serving 50M users worldwide.

Talent Mapping & Sourcing:

  • Global Talent Scouting: Help map and engage elite talent from Tier 1 tech hubs and companies worldwide. You’ll identify and connect with candidates who aren’t actively applying through thoughtful outreach and strong networking.

  • Smart Sourcing: Support the implementation of an AI-first recruitment stack. You’ll use tools, from AI agents to niche technical communities and unconventional channels, to help us find exceptional talent

  • Relationship Building: Maintain long-term relationships with passive talent globally to ensure we stay ahead of hiring needs as we continue scaling

Candidate Experience & Evaluation:

  • World-Class Candidate Experience: Own the candidate journey from the first discovery call to the final close. Ensure every interaction with EverAI, whether candidates join us or not, is clear, respectful, and high-quality

  • Interviews and Screenings: Conduct structured interviews to assess technical aptitude and cultural alignment, and provide concise, actionable summaries for Hiring Managers and Leadership

Process Innovation & Collaboration:

  • Hiring Operations: Work closely with Founders and Team Leads to improve hiring workflows, remove friction, and strengthen how we operate as we grow past 100+ employees

  • Employer Branding and other Initiatives: Contribute to creative initiatives and content that position EverAI as the #1 destination for the world’s best AI talent

Your Qualifications

Must-haves

  • Minimum 3 years of experience in recruitment, with at least 2 years in tech recruitment

  • Experience working in a start-up or scale-up environment

  • Global sourcing experience: You have a track record of helping attract talent from major tech hubs (USA, EU, LATAM, etc.)

  • You thrive in a high-trust environment where you are empowered to learn, improve processes, and make an impact

Others

🗣 Strong communication & collaborative skills (perfectly fluent in English)

🎯 Goal-oriented, ownership and commitment

⚡️ Doer mindset - we are moving fast and we need people who can find the right balance between executing, planning and strategy

🧢 Humble - willing to learn, open to feedback

🍭 #NSFW - you are comfortable hiring for products that are based on uncensored models and content

Bonus points

  • Experience in AI recruitment or familiarity with the AI space

  • Exposure to employer branding, compensation benchmarking, or broader TA initiatives

Why EverAI?

📈 Exponential Growth: From 60M users in 3 years, to 100M next — and 500M beyond

🚀 Track Record of Category-Creating Innovation: We consistently launch world-first AI applications — setting the pace, not following it

🌍 Global Impact: Top-tier user growth, real-world adoption, and cultural relevance

🧠 Proven Leadership: A senior team that’s launched, scaled, and exited & IPO’d multiple scale ups — now fully focused on reshaping AI companionship

👥 Elite Remote Team: 100% remote and built to win — world-class talent from Tier 1 tech companies, with a culture of ownership, velocity, and radical creativity

🛡️ Ethical Core: Our AI ecosystem is governed by EverGuard, our proprietary AI moderation technology, ensuring responsible development at scale

What We Offer

🏝️ Paid Time Off: 20 working days of PTO per year to recharge and reset
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Annual Gathering: A yearly in-person meetup to connect, brainstorm, and celebrate wins together
❤️‍🩹 Health & Wellness Support: Monthly allowance of100 USD for health insurance expenses & access to unlimited 1:1 sessions with psychologists and lifestyle experts through OpenUp (also available to up to three of your family members)
🏢 Co-Working Space Budget: Work from a co-working space up to twice per month (35 EUR / 40 USD per visit) to stay inspired and connected
📚 Learning Budget: Dedicated funds to support your professional growth: courses, books, conferences, events, or certifications
💻 Company Laptop & Equipment: Laptop provided + monitor budget up to 250 USD + keyboard/mouse/mic/headphones budget up to 150 USD
⚡ AI Tools Access: Premium access to ChatGPT, Hugging Face, Claude Code, and any other tool needed to excel at your job, power your ideas and workflows

🎯 Top Tier Talent Is Our Multiplier

We’re a fully remote group of A-players from Tier 1 tech, led by an exec team who’ve launched, scaled, and exited multiple companies. We move fast, and care deeply about what we build — and who we build it with.

We’re looking for exceptional talent ready to ship & distribute world-first AI products at scale, fast, and co-create with us this category-defining business.

If that’s you — reach out and apply!

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.
